notes:
BLOCKED on HELPER_MISSING: no OpenMHS driver shape can carry the primary control of the pinned arbok_driver. No driver.py or fake is submitted because the only expressible subset would be observation and reset, which the task rules forbid as a replacement for primary control. No hardware was attached or run, no upstream code was imported or executed, and this model-authored package has no human review or hardware evidence.

ENTRY SYMBOLS CONFIRMED at the pinned commit e5c66bf3577fb1cbd1ba875e039a7bf2d4b3121c: Measurement (arbok_driver/measurement.py:48), ArbokDriver (arbok_driver/arbok_driver.py:29), ReadSequence (arbok_driver/read_sequence.py:15), GettableParameterMulti (arbok_driver/parameters/gettable_parameter_multi.py:16), GettableParameter (arbok_driver/parameters/gettable_parameter.py:13). The clone is clean at that commit and was not modified.

WHY QcodesDriver CANNOT EXPRESS IT: the card's family-config/QcodesDriver is a static-scan guess. QcodesDriver binds explicit self.<name> = Parameter(...) assignments, and G7 proves them in the native class. The selected ArbokDriver creates its only Parameter dynamically with self.add_parameter('iteration', get_cmd=None, set_cmd=None) (arbok_driver/arbok_driver.py:60), and SequenceBase creates every measurement parameter through self.add_parameter(...) (arbok_driver/sequence_base.py:405-411). There is no static Parameter assignment in the class ancestry, so no explicit parameter_bindings can be cited.

WHY A DIRECT DRIVER CANNOT EXPRESS THE PRIMARY CONTROL: ArbokDriver.run(qua_program) (arbok_driver/arbok_driver.py:147-155) calls self.opx.execute(qua_program); qua_program is a QUA Program object built by Measurement.get_qua_program() under with qua.program() (arbok_driver/sequence_base.py:210-228) and passed to the native run by Measurement.compile_qua_and_run() (arbok_driver/measurement.py:525, 540-542). generate_qua_script() at sequence_base.py:227 is output-only; the clone has no parser or loader that turns a string, dict or file into a Program. OpenMHS fields carry JSON values, not a QUA Program, so a run action would have to hand the native method a type it cannot execute (for example a path or source text) and would invent a control path the upstream does not have.

WHY A MEASUREMENT CANNOT BE PRE-BUILT HONESTLY: Measurement.__init__ needs a parent ArbokDriver and a sequence_config (arbok_driver/measurement.py:48-70); the shipped configs contain Python sequence classes and parameter-type classes, for example "sequence": SquarePulse and 'type': Amplitude at arbok_driver/examples/configurations/sequence/square_pulse_confs.py:8-16, while Device needs an opx_config and divider_config (arbok_driver/device.py:14-35). These are user Python objects, not contract values. A fixed example measurement would be an invented task, and the package cannot select or construct arbitrary user sequences from a JSON input.

FRAMEWORK SCOPE: the confirmed entry Measurement is a framework class (arbok_driver/measurement.py:48) built on SequenceBase (arbok_driver/sequence_base.py:27); ReadSequence and the GettableParameter classes are framework building blocks too. The only concrete sequences and configurations are under arbok_driver/examples/, for example SquarePulse at arbok_driver/examples/sequences/square_pulse.py:14 and its config at arbok_driver/examples/configurations/sequence/square_pulse_confs.py:8; they are examples, not a shipped production measurement. Binding one would invent a task and a device configuration, and the card has no models or concrete experiment entry.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: a direct Driver with a deployment-supplied Measurement object (through backend options) was considered. It could expose reset and a thin wrapper around compile_qua_and_run, but the measurement and QUA program would still be defined by Python code outside the OpenMHS contract, so the contract would not carry the device's programmable-measurement interface; the result would be a wrapper around arbitrary operator code, not a tested integration. A string or path program loader is not an upstream API and would invent a control path.

STOP PATH: ArbokDriver itself has no stop, abort or halt method. The only cancellation in the clone is qm_job.cancel() in the measurement runner's finally block (arbok_driver/measurement_runners/measurement_runner_base.py:124-125) and opx.close() (arbok_driver/arbok_driver.py:132). Without a configured qm_job there is no stop to invoke, and a cancellation acknowledgement is not sensed quiescence.

LAST GATE OUTPUT (run 2 of at most 6, 2026-11-05T02:15:14Z, backend fake): G1 fail Layout and isolation (G1.MISSING_FILE driver.py, driver.lock.json, test_driver.py; G1.MISSING_FAKE; warning G1.NO_FACTS_MD), G2 fail Lock (G2.NO_LOCK), G3 fail Strict resolve (G3.IMPORT driver.py missing), G4-G8 skip NOT_RUN, G9 fail Repository tests (G9.MISSING test_driver.py); exit 1; failed G1 G2 G3 G9. The missing-file findings reflect that no package was authored; they are not evidence that an observation-only subset satisfies the device contract.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: no driver was implemented. The card's QcodesDriver cannot bind this dynamic-instrument interface, and a direct Driver cannot carry the QUA Program object that is the primary control. No catalogue_requests are made because no x-cap id was used. task.json was not edited.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block against arbok_driver.py, sequence_base.py, measurement.py, device.py, the examples and measurement_runner_base.py at the pin; it matches the readiness evidence (no add_parameter profile, and a QUA program builder rather than an instrument). ArbokDriver creates its only Parameter with add_parameter (arbok_driver.py:60) and SequenceBase creates every measurement parameter the same way (sequence_base.py:405-411), so QcodesDriver cannot bind them; the primary control is run(qua_program) (arbok_driver.py:147-155) with a QUA Program that get_qua_program builds in Python from user sequence classes (sequence_base.py:210-228; measurement.py:519-543), which no JSON input can carry; the only cancellation is qm_job.cancel() in a runner's finally block (measurement_runner_base.py:123-125). Every citation in the author's notes shows what it claims. No file was edited (the gate re-run only regenerated check-report.json); the gate fails G1, G2, G3 and G9 because no package was authored (stable digest sha256:7eed08badde1ce96120483ac85f5113600aa8fbaf4407e0b68aa5f1b7b5fad79, unchanged). For the human reviewer: The device is a Quantum Machines OPX reached through the external qm package; arbok is the measurement framework on top. Every measurement is user Python code (SubSequence classes and their configs), so no fixed OpenMHS contract exists; the skip proposal routes the card out of the driver waves.
